correctness.rationale: From a two-Bernoulli coupling, the clear-clear probability is (1-u)(1-v)(1+α min(r_u,r_v)), so the all-clear Markov path product is B times the factors indexed by adjacent edge minima. For edge-minimum order statistics b_j, path degree <=2 implies b_j>=r_{ceil(j/2)}; the induced subgraph on ranks >k is a forest implying b_k<=r_k. Coordinatewise product comparison gives both bounds, realized by explicit alternating large-small and monotone or single-peaked paths. Coefficientwise monotonicity of elementary symmetric polynomials gives nonnegative coefficients of the width in α, strictly increasing for distinct n>=3. Independent rational Markov recursion checked 23648 permutations through n=7 and all α in {0,1/4,1/2,1}, including the exact four-level bounds 454/625 and 3917/5000. These finite tests are not the arbitrary-n proof.
